instruction: Set the default font of this document to Courier New.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.press("down", presses=40, interval=0.01); time.sleep(1); pyautogui.scroll(-2)
import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully inserted a 7x5 table at cursor position using Table > Insert Table dialog. Set columns to 7 and rows to 5, then clicked Insert.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate LibreOffice Writer menus, open Insert Table dialog, configure column/row counts, insert tables at cursor position.
metadata.task_rationale: Tests document-level formatting change (default font). The model demonstrated menu navigation and dialog interaction in Writer, so modifying the default font via Tools > Options or Format > Character should be achievable.
metadata.explanation: Custom getter reads the saved document and extracts the default font from the Normal style, document defaults XML, or most common font across paragraphs. Metric compares the actual font name against expected 'Courier New' (case-insensitive).

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts default font using three fallback methods: Normal style font, docDefaults XML rFonts, and most common font across paragraphs. Method 1 (Normal style) is the primary and correct location where LibreOffice Writer stores the default font in .docx format.
Metric correctly handles expected parameter — accesses expected.get('expected_font') directly, which is correct since get_rule returns config['rules'] = {'expected_font': 'Courier New'}.
Case-insensitive comparison in metric is appropriate for font name matching.
Postconfig correctly saves the file (Ctrl+S) before the getter reads it, ensuring fresh state.
Full coverage: the single instruction requirement (set default font to Courier New) is completely verified.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: Method 3 fallback (most common font across paragraphs) could give misleading results if the default font style was changed but existing text was not reflowed. Consider prioritizing style-based detection more heavily or adding a warning when falling back to Method 3.
